title: Notice the Thought–Action Loop
subtitle: A symptom, the meaning you give it, and what you do next can influence one another.
description: This is not about thinking pain away. Pain is real. The goal is to notice when an automatic conclusion changes stress, confidence, or behaviour before you have considered the whole situation.

sections.title: Notice the first conclusion
sections.description: Think about a recent familiar symptom change. What did your mind predict, and what did you do next?

fields.label: Which reactions have you noticed?
options: I immediately assumed I had caused damage
I became tense, guarded, or worried
I stopped more activity than I had planned
I pushed through to prove I was okay
I considered the pattern and adjusted calmly
I asked for help because the symptoms were new or concerning

fields.label: What was the first thought or prediction you noticed?
fields.placeholder: For example: ‘I have undone my progress’ or ‘This will never settle’...

sections.title: Choose a more useful next step
sections.description: A thought is not automatically a fact. Consider the pattern, your function, the response over time, and the clinical guidance you already have.

fields.label: Which response could help you gather better information?
options: Try a manageable version of the activity
Review the familiar pattern before assuming the worst
Modify the amount without abandoning movement
Use the plan already discussed with my practitioner
Seek assessment for something new, severe, or concerning
Remember evidence of capacity I have already built

fields.label: Complete the loop: When I notice ___, my first thought is ___. A useful next step may be ___.
fields.placeholder: Describe one real situation and the response you want to practise...

successMessage: Your map is complete. You are not being asked to dismiss symptoms—only to pause, consider the whole pattern, and choose the next useful action.
